Gates: each 600 < 1500 and 600+600 = 1200 < 1500 (300 s slack). Scored: 9000, 900, 900 each < 11100 and 9000+900+900 = 10800 < 11100 (300 s slack). This satisfies the workbook row, the internal annotation (sum of judges 1200+10800 = 12000 < 13200) and quality-checks.md ### 11. test.sh, tools/score.py, tools/restart_mcp.py, tests/Dockerfile, environment/Dockerfile and scoring.toml are byte-identical to the frozen template (cmp/diff), so the task changed no budget; per AGENTS.md and REVIEW_POLICY no unmeasured change is warranted. LIVENESS: test.sh:116-125 polls 120 x (probe_ready + sleep 0.25); probe_ready uses urlopen(timeout=2) on /api/health then / (test.sh:48-50): ~30 s nominally; worst case for a hung-but-accepting server ~120 x 4.3 s = ~516 s, then exit 0 with the zero reward already written (write_zero_reward at test.sh:59 before anything). 516 s + cp -a/chown + 12600 s is ~13116 s plus copy time, inside 13200 only marginally; reachable only by a pathological app and the zero reward is pre-written, so a P3 note, not a defect. restart_app is bounded by restart_mcp.py:11 HELPER_TIMEOUT_SEC = 55 inside the 9000 s functional judge (helper's own readiness wait ~30 s nominal). Agent 7200 s is ample (lesson 3: the target builder typically builds in 5-10 min). build_timeout 600 s covers the template-identical environment Dockerfile (4 apt packages + 2 pinned npm globals). LONG ENOUGH, NOT MEASURED: raw-evidence-index.json scope reads 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent', and every entry is a scripted golden run labelled 'Not a configured judge run, Oracle grade, model score or judge-duration measurement'. The functional judge must, in one batched claude-code + z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx session of 9000 s, run the gate plus 14 protocols (Z,S,M,L,C,B,N,T,U,K,R,V,A,D; functional/prompt.md:33-59) for 44 criteria: 11+ UI adds on two jobs plus refused-input attempts, ~25 ordinary moves, many independent contexts (Mei Lin, Ingrid, Bill, Aud, Tomas, Noor, Lena, anonymous), 10+ timed observations each up to 15 s + 2 s settle with up to 3 attempts (prompt.md:21), ~24 replays in protocol R alone (7 request kinds x Observer and candidate plus 10 anonymous), ~6 in B, candidate-page request capture, and a restart. A plausible estimate is several hundred MCP tool calls, i.e. roughly 15-30 s per call available: feasible but unproven. Polish is tighter: 900 s for the gate (add, reload, independent Observer context), opening a job, adding up to twelve cards through the UI to make the board scroll (polish/judge.toml:25), a live-board timed observation, two Noor conversation legs, an abort/offline failed send and a multi-sign-in session-resume row (polish/judge.toml:51, 61): on the order of 100+ tool calls at ~7-9 s each. Visual 900 s for 5 Likert observations is plausible. Lesson 11: a judge timeout zeroes a dimension; prompt.md:61 makes an exhausted budget return binary 0 'NOT EXERCISED', so a too-short budget would attribute harness failure to the submission (a functional zero also fails the floor). Per REVIEW_POLICY 'Workload is measured, not inferred from a timeout number', so I neither pass nor fail 'long enough' on an estimate: the nesting half is verified, the duration half is Not exercised and is a required missing measurement (risk = true). Other lessons checked for this row: 7/14 timed-observation repeat rule is bounded (at most two more attempts, prompt.md:21); 10 assembled functional prompt ~22.3 KB + 1.9 KB app_context + ~27 KB criteria = ~51 KB < 128 KB; 11 judge timeout/infra crash risk is relevant and unmeasured.
counterexample: Not a demonstrated defect (no measurement either way). Plausible failure: the golden or a strong conforming app is graded by the configured GLM judge; the polish judge spends most of its 900 s adding twelve cards and switching sign-ins and times out before the failed-send/session-resume rows, or the 9000 s functional session runs out during R/A/D, so those rows return 0 'NOT EXERCISED' or the dimension errors, lowering Oracle below 1 for a harness reason. A dead app fails the gate early and finishes far under budget, so the risk is one-sided against correct apps.
suggested_fix: Before clearance, run the full configured verifier (test.sh with claude-code + glm-5.3-flashx) on the golden at least once and record per-dimension wall time from the rewardkit logs against 600/600/9000/900/900; if polish or functional runs near or over budget, first cut redundant browser work (e.g. fewer cards to force scroll, fewer replay kinds in R), and only with a recorded reason and authorization consider a timeout change kept below five hours and still nested.
